newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta extends Megawati office closure deadline.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta extends Megawati office closure deadline.

text.p: A Jakarta official on Thursday extended the deadline for ousted minority party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri to close her office, but there was no hint of an easing in government hostility towards her political activities.

Tarto Sudiro, a Megawati supporter and member of parliament, told Reuters that a letter addressed to Megawati from East Jakarta Mayor Sudarsono set a new deadline of around 11:30 a.m. (0430 GMT) on Friday.
Megawati later emerged from a meeting with advisers at the new headquarters and declined to answer questions about her group's next step. "Just wait until tomorrow," she said.
The afternoon daily Harian Terbit newspaper quoted Sudarsono as saying the letter was Megawati's final warning.
"If the office is not yet closed today, tommorrow I will seal it," he was quoted as saying on Thursday morning.

A judge, meanwhile, adjourned hearings on the lawsuit filed by Megawati against the government, military and political rivals over her June ejection as leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
Judge I Gde Ketut Sukarata adjourned the suit on Thursday after after the defence questioned the court's jurisdiction.
"The court is adjourned until October 10...when we will hand down a decision on whether this court has the authority to hear this case," the judge said.

Megawati had set up a new office for her faction of the PDI after police raided the official party headquarters on July 27, evicting her supporters and sparking the worst riots in the city of some 10 million people in more than two decades.

The authorities have warned her against continuing her political activities, and Sudarsono sent a letter on Monday giving Megawati's faction 72 hours to close the office, saying it violated residential zoning laws.
The municipality delivered another letter on Thursday morning setting a new deadline of 24 hours from receipt of the note.

"If you do not implement in a short time what has been ordered, the government of Jakarta, represented by the mayor of East Jakarta, will implement the closure and you will bear the consequences," the letter said.
Megawati, daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno, attended a ceremonial meal at the two-storey suburban building just hours before the original deadline on Thursday.
She thanked some 250 supporters for attending the meal and said the office was a "temporary" one because she was seeking reinstatement as PDI leader through the courts.
Political analysts have said the government wanted her out of the PDI leadership for fear she would draw votes away from the ruling Golkar in general elections in May next year.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI, Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only groups legally entitled to contest the elections.
